no_trade.reason: Visa is a phenomenal business with >50% net margins and >60% ROE. However, trading at a 31x P/E multiple right beneath technical range resistance ($371.16) with fundamental fair value starting at $385 offers insufficient risk/reward to initiate a new position today.
no_trade.what_would_reopen: A confirmed, high-volume breakout above the $371.16 resistance level, or a meaningful pullback toward moving average support at $344 or range support at $317 to improve the margin of safety.

invalidation_conditions: Sustained price breakdown below the 856.05 structural support level on abnormal volume.
Trailing twelve-month FCF drops below $8B, indicating a severe reversal of customer advances.
Continued sequential equity declines in Q3 2026 without formal announcements of shareholder return programs.
proposal.thesis: GEV presents a compelling valuation dislocation, trading at ~20x TTM FCF on the back of $12.64B in TTM free cash flow. While GAAP EPS volatility and short-term technical weakness have clouded the narrative, this massive cash generation likely stems from structural working-capital advantages. However, unresolved concerns surrounding an unexplained $1.96B equity contraction in Q2 2026 and the risk of a working-capital reversal require conservative sizing. We go long near structural support, anticipating that upcoming earnings will confirm the durability of FCF and clarify capital return programs.
premortem_top_risks: The recent FCF surge proves to be a temporary working-capital pull-forward, leading to severe valuation multiple compression as the FCF denominator collapses.
The unexplained Q2 equity contraction was masking actual balance-sheet deterioration or hidden OCI losses rather than capital returns.
The technical setup breaks down as the market rejects the fundamental cash flow narrative and stop-loss selling cascades.
The bear thesis fails because the cash flow model is structurally durable, and the market re-rates the stock upward on undeniable cash yields.
